threat_event: Leaked long-lived CI/CD cloud key is used to download the document bucket (including W-9s with Social Security numbers) and copy a database snapshot
threat_source: Cybercriminal using credentials stolen by information-stealing malware
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Static administrator key created in March 2024, never rotated, copied to the contractor's unmanaged personal laptop; no object-level read logging; no alerts on bulk downloads or snapshot copies
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-01 document bucket and database; SYS-02; all 45 customers' vendor data; BP-01, BP-02
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a); 45(n) unfairness); Customer DPA (contract) (72-hour notice); Fla. Stat. 501.171(2) (reasonable measures by a third-party agent)
existing_controls: Bucket is private; storage encrypted at rest; MFA on human console accounts
treatment_plan: Replace the key with short-lived federated credentials scoped to deployment and delete it; remove the copy from the contractor's laptop; object read logging, database audit logging, and threat detection alerts; quarterly check for long-lived keys

threat_event: An engineer's or the contractor's cloud administrator account is misused or taken over to read, change, or delete all customer data and its backups
threat_source: Insider or external attacker with a stolen session
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 5 people hold full administrator rights; no read-only or deploy-only roles; snapshots in the same account; no alerting on destructive actions
existing_controls: MFA on console accounts; per-person accounts
treatment_plan: Create read-only, deploy-only, and break-glass administrator roles; remove standing administrator rights from everyone except the CTO and Senior Software Engineer; copy backups to a separate account with write-once retention

threat_event: Production database extracts on laptops are exposed through malware, theft, or loss
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Engineers copy production extracts to laptops for debugging, including the contractor's personal laptop with no company encryption, antivirus, or patching evidence
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-08; contractor laptop; customer vendor data
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a); 45(n) unfairness) (FTC guidance: don't use personal information when it's not necessary); Customer DPA (contract)
existing_controls: Company laptops encrypted and MSP-managed
treatment_plan: Stop production extracts; delete existing extracts and confirm in writing; synthetic test data set; contractor works only on a company-issued laptop

threat_event: Authorization flaw lets one customer's users see another customer's vendors and documents
threat_source: Customer user or external attacker probing the API
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Tenant isolation enforced only in application code; no automated cross-tenant tests; no penetration test ever
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a); 45(n) unfairness) (FTC guidance: continuously validate access to data); Customer DPA (contract)
existing_controls: Every query filtered by tenant ID; code review on each change
treatment_plan: Automated cross-tenant tests in CI that block a merge on failure; first penetration test focused on tenant isolation (2027-01)

threat_event: Tax IDs sent to the AI model provider and to the error tracking service are exposed in a breach at either vendor
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Full W-9 text with Social Security numbers is sent for extraction; error payloads include extracted text; neither vendor was reviewed
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-05; SYS-06; vendors' Social Security numbers
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a); 45(n) unfairness); N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a); deception) (website: tax IDs never leave our platform); Customer DPA (contract)
existing_controls: TLS to both vendors; error logs kept 14 days
treatment_plan: Mask Social Security numbers before text goes to the model provider (extract only the last 4 digits and the TIN type); redact tax IDs from error payloads; vendor reviews in P09

threat_event: A customer, prospect, or regulator finds that public security statements, the security exhibit, or questionnaire answers are false
threat_source: Customer audit, prospect due diligence, SOC 2 auditor, or FTC inquiry
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Website says tax IDs never leave the platform; security exhibit promises annual penetration tests and 30-day backups; questionnaires answered 'SOC 2 compliant'; no review of statements against practice
affected_asset_or_process: Company reputation; all customer contracts; sales pipeline
existing_controls: None
treatment_plan: Correct the website and product page claims; send corrected answers to prospects who received questionnaires in the last 12 months; CTO approval of every questionnaire answer; quarterly statement review

threat_event: A faulty script, mistaken delete, or attacker removes or overwrites stored documents that cannot be recovered
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Document bucket versioning is off; no copy outside the production account
existing_controls: Storage durability; code review
treatment_plan: Turn on versioning now; replicate to a separate backup account with write-once retention of 35 days

threat_event: Database or application recovery takes far longer than the 4-hour RTO after an outage or destructive incident
threat_source: Cloud service failure or the destructive events in R-002 and R-007
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No restore test ever; no recovery runbook; about 40% of production built by hand in the console
regulatory_driver: Customer MSA (contract) (99.5% uptime target); N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a); deception) (security exhibit backup promise)
existing_controls: Point-in-time recovery and snapshots exist
treatment_plan: First timed restore test by 2026-10-31; short contingency plan and recovery runbook; bring all production resources into infrastructure code

threat_event: Customer notice after an incident misses the 72-hour DPA clock or the Florida 10-day third-party-agent clock
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No incident response plan before P08; no customer security contact list; no notice templates
regulatory_driver: Customer DPA (contract) (72-hour notice); Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)(a) (third-party agent notice within 10 days)
existing_controls: Cyber insurance with breach hotline and panel counsel
treatment_plan: Adopt the P08 runbook; build the customer security contact list; counsel-approved notice templates; tabletop 2026-11-12

threat_event: Former employee or contractor uses access that was never removed
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Offboarding is ad hoc; admin console and support desk accounts sit outside single sign-on; no account reviews
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-01 admin console; SYS-07 support desk; SYS-02
existing_controls: Suite account disabled on the last day by the MSP
treatment_plan: Offboarding checklist covering every system; move the admin console and support desk behind single sign-on; monthly account reconciliation

threat_event: Phishing takes over a staff suite account and uses single sign-on to reach the repository, support desk, and CRM
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No awareness training; MFA by authenticator app push, which can be fatigued or relayed; single sign-on opens CI secrets in the repository
existing_controls: Suite MFA for all users; MSP email filtering
treatment_plan: Awareness training and quarterly phishing simulations; number matching for MFA; hardware security keys for the CTO and both engineers

threat_event: MSP global administrator account in the suite is compromised and used to grant repository access and reach CI secrets
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: MSP holds 2 global administrator accounts; MSP contract has no security incident notice or access review terms; single sign-on opens the repository
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-03; SYS-02; then SYS-01 through the CI key
existing_controls: MFA on MSP administrator accounts
treatment_plan: Annual MSP security questionnaire; contract terms for 24-hour incident notice and named administrators; repository access only for named engineers with hardware keys

threat_event: A known vulnerability in a library or container base image is exploited in the public web application
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 14 High dependency alerts older than 30 days; container images not scanned; no remediation time limits
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a); 45(n) unfairness) (FTC guidance: update and patch third-party software)
existing_controls: Repository dependency alerts
treatment_plan: Image scanning in CI; time limits (Critical 7 days, High 30 days); clear the 14 overdue alerts

threat_event: Credential stuffing takes over a customer administrator account and downloads that customer's W-9s
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: MFA is optional for customer users, including administrators who can see every W-9 in their tenant
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a); 45(n) unfairness) (FTC guidance: insist on complex and unique passwords; guard against brute force attacks)
existing_controls: Lockout after 5 failed attempts; hashed passwords
treatment_plan: Require MFA for customer administrators; offer it to all users; alert on many failed sign-ins

threat_event: AI extraction misreads a certificate so a non-compliant vendor shows as compliant (or the reverse), and a customer relies on it
threat_source: Model error on unusual or poor-quality documents
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No accuracy testing before release; customers can accept extracted fields without review; '99% accuracy' claim unsupported
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-06; BP-02; customer decisions on site access
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a); deception) (accuracy claim); Customer DPA (contract)
existing_controls: Reviewer screen shows the document next to the extracted fields
treatment_plan: Accuracy test set and thresholds (P10); reviewer must confirm coverage limits and expiry dates; withdraw the 99% claim

threat_event: A customer finds that the AI model provider processes its data without notice, a DPA, or retention limits
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Provider added 2026-04-20 on click-through terms; not on the sub-processor list; provider's standard terms allow 30-day retention for abuse monitoring
regulatory_driver: Customer DPA (contract) (30-day sub-processor notice); N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a); deception)
existing_controls: Provider's API terms say inputs are not used for training
treatment_plan: Sign the provider's DPA with zero-retention terms; add it to the sub-processor list; notify customers with a 30-day objection window

threat_event: Data of terminated customers is kept past the 60-day deletion promise and is exposed or found in an audit
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No deletion process; 2 former customers' data kept 5 and 11 months after termination
regulatory_driver: Customer DPA (contract) (60-day deletion); N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a); deception)
existing_controls: None
treatment_plan: Delete the 2 former tenants after confirming no legal hold; deletion runbook with a certificate to the customer

threat_event: Staff use view-as-customer to browse a customer's vendors without a support need
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No customer approval, ticket link, or session log for view-as-customer
regulatory_driver: Customer DPA (contract) (data used only to provide the service)
existing_controls: Only 4 staff have admin console accounts
treatment_plan: Ticket-linked, time-limited sessions with a session log; monthly review

threat_event: The CTO is unavailable for weeks, stalling operations, recovery, and incident response
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Only the CTO knows the whole production setup; no runbooks; root account tied to the CTO's phone
existing_controls: Senior Software Engineer has partial knowledge
treatment_plan: Recovery runbook; Senior Software Engineer leads the first restore test; emergency account held by the Chief Executive Officer

threat_event: Malicious text hidden in an uploaded document manipulates the AI extraction into marking a vendor compliant
threat_source: Vendor or attacker uploading a crafted PDF
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Document text goes straight into the prompt; no check of extracted values against rules
existing_controls: Customer reviewer can see the document
treatment_plan: Treat document text as data in the prompt; rule checks on dates and limits; reviewer confirmation for any status change (P10)

threat_event: A company laptop is lost or stolen
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Laptops travel; some hold cached customer data
existing_controls: Full-disk encryption and remote wipe through the MSP
treatment_plan: Accepted by the CTO 2026-09-15: encryption makes the data unusable to a thief; existing controls are sufficient

threat_event: A cloud regional outage stops the platform beyond the uptime target
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Single region
existing_controls: Provider's multi-zone database and container services
treatment_plan: Accepted by the Chief Executive Officer 2026-09-15: a second region costs more than the service credits at risk; revisit at the SOC 2 Type 2

threat_event: The SOC 2 Type 1 is late or has exceptions, and the anchor customer renewal or the 2 prospects are lost
threat_source: Readiness gaps not closed in time
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Many controls new or not yet operating (P09); one person runs the program part-time
affected_asset_or_process: Revenue (about 30% from the anchor customers); sales pipeline
existing_controls: Readiness plan in P09
treatment_plan: Monthly readiness review with the Chief Executive Officer; engage the CPA firm by 2026-12-15; compliance automation tool for evidence collection

threat_event: A leaked email delivery API key is used to send phishing to vendors from the company's sending domain
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Key created in 2024, stored as an environment variable and in the contractor's local file, never rotated
existing_controls: Sending domain authentication records
treatment_plan: Rotate the key and store it in a secrets manager; send-volume alert

threat_event: The cloud root account is taken over through the shared vault entry or the CTO's personal phone
threat_source: Attacker with vault access or the phone
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Root password in a vault entry shared with all engineers and the contractor; MFA device is a personal phone
existing_controls: MFA on the root account
treatment_plan: Move the root password to a vault entry only the Chief Executive Officer and CTO can open; hardware security key for root MFA; alert on any root sign-in
